source_text:
Στίχ. ιε΄, ις΄. Κεκράξατε· παρέδωνε γὰρ Κύριος ὑμῖν τὴν πόλιν.
(70) Διατί τὴν Ἰεριχὼ ἀναθεματισθῆναι προσέταξε; Πρώτην ταύτην εἷλον πόλιν μετὰ τὸ διαβῆναι31 τὸν ποταμόν. Ὥσπερ τοίνυν προσέταξεν αὐτοὺς τῶν καρπῶν προσφέρειν τὰς ἀπαρχὰς, οὕτως ἐκέλευσε τὰ τῶν σκύλων προσενεγκεῖν ἀκροθίνια. Πρὸς δὲ τούτοις καὶ γυμνάζει αὐτοὺς διὰ τούτων τῶν νόμων, ὥστε τοὺς ἀναγκαίους νόμους τηρεῖν. Τὴν οἰκείαν δὲ αὐτοῖς ἐπιδεικνὺς δύναμιν, τὴν πρώτην πόλιν δίχα ὅπλων καὶ μηχανημάτων ἑλεῖν παρεσκεύασε, καὶ μόνῃ κατέλυσε τῇ τῶν σαλπίγγων ἠχῇ· ἵνʼ ὅταν ἡττηθῶσι παραταττόμενοι, γνῶσιν, ὡς αὐτοὶ παρέσχον τῆς ἥττης τὰς ἀφορμὰς, τῶν θείων νόμων καταφρονήσαντες.
thought_title: Why Jericho was devoted to destruction
orientation: Origen is commenting on Joshua 6:15-16, where the people shout and the Lord gives them the city, and he asks why Joshua commanded Jericho to be devoted to destruction.
pass_a_gloss: Verse 15, 16. You shouted; for the Lord has handed over to you the city. (70) Why did he command Jericho to be devoted to destruction? They took this city first after crossing the river. Just as therefore he commanded them to offer the firstfruits of the crops, so he ordered them to offer the first spoils of the plunder. And in addition to these things he also trains them through these laws, so that they keep the necessary laws. And showing them his own power, he prepared the first city to be taken without weapons and siege engines, and he destroyed it by the sound of the trumpets alone; so that whenever they are defeated in battle, they may know that they themselves provided the causes of the defeat, having despised the divine laws.

choices.why: Glossary term; renders the act of devoting a city and its contents to destruction as belonging to God
Glossary term for firstfruits offered to God from produce
Glossary term for the best spoils of war offered to God
Renders σκύλων as plunder or spoils taken from a conquered enemy, consistent with the glossary's προνομὴν
Renders the military machines used in siege warfare, contrasting with divine power
Renders the middle/passive participle of παρατάσσω meaning being drawn up in battle line, i.e., engaging in battle

bible_refs.note: Κεκράξατε· παρέδωνε γὰρ Κύριος ὑμῖν τὴν πόλιν

pass_b_english: "Shout! For the Lord has handed the city over to you" (Joshua 6:16).

Why did he command that Jericho be devoted to destruction? This was the first city they took after crossing the river. Just as he commanded them to offer the firstfruits of the crops, so he ordered them to offer the first spoils of the plunder. In addition to this, he trains them through these laws so that they will keep the necessary laws. And to show them his own power, he arranged for the first city to be taken without weapons or siege engines, and he destroyed it by the sound of trumpets alone—so that when they are defeated in battle, they will know that they themselves provided the causes of their defeat by despising the divine laws.

problems.quote: he trains them through these laws so that they will keep the necessary laws
problems.why: Ambiguous whether 'he' is God, Joshua, or Moses; referent unclear
problems.fix: Clarify 'God trains them' or 'the law trains them'

problems.quote: they will know that they themselves provided the causes of their defeat
problems.why: Sudden shift to 'when they are defeated'—who is 'they'? Israel or enemies?
problems.fix: Clarify 'when Israel is defeated in later battles'

problems.quote: he trains them through these laws so that they will keep the necessary laws
problems.why: Circular and redundant; 'laws' repeated awkwardly, possibly mistranslated
problems.fix: Revise to 'he trains them by these rules to observe his commandments'

edits.old: In addition to this, he trains them through these laws so that they will keep the necessary laws.
edits.new: In addition to this, God trains them through these laws so that they will keep the necessary laws.

edits.old: so that when they are defeated in battle, they will know that they themselves provided the causes of their defeat by despising the divine laws.
edits.new: so that when Israel is defeated in later battles, they will know that they themselves provided the causes of their defeat by despising the divine laws.

fixed: Clarified 'he' as 'God' to remove ambiguity about the referent.
Clarified 'they' as 'Israel' to remove ambiguity about who is defeated.
